what_its_for: Testosterone enanthate is used to treat low testosterone levels (hypogonadism) in men when the body does not make enough testosterone on its own. It may also be used to treat certain types of breast cancer in women, and in some cases to help transgender men during hormone therapy. Testosterone is a natural hormone that is important for sexual development, muscle growth, bone strength, and overall energy levels.
how_to_take: This medication is given as an injection into a muscle (usually the buttock or thigh) or under the skin, depending on the product your doctor prescribed. It may be given by your doctor or nurse at a clinic, or you may be taught how to give the injection to yourself at home. Always use a new, sterile needle and syringe for each injection. Rotate the injection site each time to avoid soreness or skin problems. Never share needles or syringes with anyone else. Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions carefully on exactly how to give the injection.
dosing: The dose and how often you take this medication depends on your condition, your age, and how your body responds to treatment. For low testosterone in adults, a common dose is 50 to 400 mg injected every 2 to 4 weeks, but your doctor will decide the right dose for you. For the Xyosted auto-injector, the usual dose is 75 mg injected under the skin once a week. Do not change your dose or how often you inject without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to find out when you should give your next injection. Do not double up or give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Try to keep all your scheduled appointments so your doses stay on track.
storage: Store testosterone enanthate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not freeze it. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. If you notice that the liquid looks cloudy, has changed color, or has particles floating in it, do not use it — contact your pharmacist. Dispose of used needles and syringes safely in an approved sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while using this medication, as it can worsen side effects and affect your hormone levels. Do not smoke, as it can interfere with how well the medication works. Avoid contact sports or activities that could cause injury to the injection site right after giving yourself a shot. Do not share this medication with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should avoid any skin contact with the injection site area of someone using testosterone, as it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: chest pain, shortness of breath, or signs of a blood clot such as leg pain or swelling; signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, weakness, or trouble speaking; severe mood changes, depression, or thoughts of harming yourself; painful or prolonged erections lasting more than 4 hours (priapism); signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; swelling of the ankles or feet; high blood pressure; sleep problems or loud snoring (sleep apnea); frequent or difficult urination; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvements within a few weeks, such as better energy, mood, and sex drive. However, it can take 3 to 6 months to feel the full effects of testosterone therapy, including improvements in muscle strength and bone density. Your doctor will check your testosterone blood levels regularly to make sure the treatment is working and to adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: Older men (over 65 years): Use with caution. Older adults may be at higher risk for side effects such as prostate problems, heart issues, and sleep apnea. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children and teenagers: This medication should only be used under close medical supervision in young patients, as it can affect bone growth and development. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding: This medication should NOT be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding, as it can cause serious harm to the baby. Patients with heart, liver, or kidney disease: Use with caution and close monitoring, as testosterone can cause fluid retention and worsen these conditions. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all the medications you are taking, including vitamins and herbal supplements, before starting testosterone therapy.
